Order Order

By invoking the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Cr. P.C., the petitioner is seeking quashing of the order dated 08.03.2022 passed by the learned Adhoc Additional District &
Sessions Judge, FTSC (POCSO Act & Rape Cases), Rayagada in T.R. Case No.78 of 2020/T.R. Case No.05 of 2022, whereby the learned Court below has framed the charges against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 376(3)/506/109 of the IPC r/w Section 4 r/w Section 3(a)/4(2) of the POCSO Act, 2012.
2.

sentences.text:
The petitioner in paragraph-6 of the petition has contended as under:
"That, since the charge has been framed on 08.03.2022 and the witnesses have been examined since 02.08.2023 and since then no progress in the trial and the petitioner having no fault running to Court since long, in spite of that there is no evidence against her to implicate in this alleged crime."
3.
Mr. Dhal, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that all the witnesses in the present case have already been examined.
None of the witnesses have whispered a single word against the petitioner.
Despite that the trial Court is not concluding the trial.
Although he has challenged the order of charge, but he would not press the present petition.
Rather, he prays before this Court for Binati Kandhapani vs State Of Odisha ....

5. With the aforementioned observation, the CRLMC is disposed of.
